name: Maridan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Tryon 1974, Daly Family Languages, Australia (PL C-32, full text read via ANU repository): Maridan treated as a Marithiel dialect; no stress statement anywhere in the volume.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. Maridan Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_zmd_swadesh-1, uploaded 2010, no source stated; forms match Tryon's Maridan wordlist).

Green, Ian. 1989. Marrithiyel: a language of the Daly River region of Australia's Northern Territory. PhD thesis, ANU. xiv+410 pp. sec. 1.4 'Dialects and Surrounding Languages' pp. 8-9 (notes 5-7 p. 13); sec. 2.1.3 'Word Stress' pp. 33-39; note 7 p. 101.
sources.note: For MARRITHIYEL only: primary stress on the first syllable of the stem, secondary on the second syllable thereafter; class prefixes do not attract stress unless lexicalised; reduplicated roots each take a primary stress; in verbs primary stress on the first syllable of the complex verb stem, otherwise on the first syllable of the verb. On Maridan: Marrithiyel speakers name 'Marridan' (coolibah-tree language) as a dialect of 'one language'; Green 'was not able to work with the few remaining identifiable Marridan speakers'; second-hand information that Marridan neutralises /l/ vs /r/ in some wo…

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 1981. The phonology and morphology of Marrithiyel: a preliminary study. MA thesis, ANU. sec. 1.3 p. 3; sec. 2.3 'Word Stress' pp. 26-32.
sources.note: Stress section is Marrithiyel data only (same stem-initial rule; superseded by Green 1989). On Maridan: 'Tryon's reasons for identifying Maridan as a dialect are rather sketchy and none of my informants believe that there are any differences between Marrithiyel and the language spoken by the Maridan. They claim that the term Maridan is simply geographical.. There are few Maridan people left.'

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid mari1422 'Maridan' (with langdoc reference list) and mari1424 'Marithiel'.
sources.note: Bibliographic only. mari1422: meds = Tryon 1968 (a wordlist or less, 1 p.); AES extinct; 8 refs, none descriptive. mari1424 (Marithiel): meds = Green 1989 long grammar, Green 1981, Tryon 1974, Dixon 1968, Stanner 1938-39, Stanner 1937.

sources.citation: Mansfield, John & Ian Green. 2021. Fricative contrasts and neutralization in Marri Tjevin. Australian Journal of Linguistics 41(2): 220-261 (author accepted MS).
sources.note: No Marri Dan data: sec. 3 'Very little is known about Marri Dan and Marramaninjsji (but see Tryon 1974)'. Its accent statements concern Marri Tjevin.

sources.citation: Nordlinger, Rachel. 2017. The languages of the Daly River region (Northern Australia). In Fortescue, Mithun & Evans (eds), The Oxford Handbook of Polysynthesis, 782-807 (AM); Bicevskis, Katie. 2023. A grammatical description of Marri Ngarr. PhD UniMelb; Ford, Lysbeth. 1998. A description of the Emmi language. PhD ANU; Mansfield, John. 2022. Word prominence in polysynthetic Australian languages (PsyArXiv).
sources.note: Nothing on Maridan: Nordlinger lists 'Marridan' only in the family table; Bicevskis mentions 'Marri Dan' only as a neighbouring country; Ford 1998 and Mansfield 2022 do not mention it.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1974. Daly family languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32. Canberra: ANU. Chapter 4c 'Maridan', pp. 102-103 (also ch. 4 'Marithiel' pp. 70-93).
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 4c (2 pp., pp. 120-121 re-rendered and read against the scan) has no phoneme list and no suprasegmental statement; it says Maridan 'morphology and syntax are identical in every respect to that described above for Marithiel' and that 'Maridan and Marithiel can for all practical purposes be considered synonymous', the only recorded difference being Marithiel /l/ ~ Maridan /r/. The Marithiel chapter's 4.2 Phonemes (p. 72) is a tentative segment list. Book-wide a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits for stress/accent/prosod/intonation/syllab.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1968. The Daly River languages: a survey. In Aguas & Tryon, Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3, 21-49. Pacific Linguistics A-14. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey with comparative wordlist; 'Maredan' is item 10 (Brinken N.57 'has four dialects: Marithiel, Maretyabin, Nganygit, and Maredan'); zero hits for stress/accent/phonolog in the volume. This is the only reference Glottolog lists as descriptive (a wordlist or less).
sources.venue: Aguas & Tryon, Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3

sources.citation: Green, Ian & Rachel Nordlinger (eds). The Daly Languages (Australia) website, 'Marri Dan' page (id=15).
sources.note: Nothing: 'Details for this language will soon be available.' Recordings/field notes: 'No resources listed.' Key Published Resources: Tryon 1974 ch. 4c pp. 102-103 only. Alt names Murindan, Nordanimin; spellings Maredan, Maridan, Meradan; dialects with Marrithiyel, Marri Tjevin, Marri Ammu.

sources.citation: Hoddinott, W. G. (with F. M. Kofod). Grammar of Marithiel, in progress per Tryon 1974 p. 70; a Marrisjabin grammar 'due for completion shortly' per Green 1989 p. 7 - apparently never published; possibly AIATSIS manuscript.

sources.note: If it exists as an AIATSIS ms it is the only other Brinken-dialect grammar of the 1970s-80s and could carry a stress note; no record located online.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. Daly River field tapes and notes (1960s-70s), AIATSIS audio collection; the Maridan wordlist of Tryon 1968/1974 was elicited from these.
